source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Founding study. Verbal compound remote associate problems. After each correct solve, people pressed insight or no insight. Exp 1 fMRI and Exp 2 EEG.
numbers: Exp1 N=13 fMRI: solved 59% of problems; 56% (SD 18.2) of solutions rated insight, 41% (SD 18.9) no insight, 2% other. Exp2 N=19 EEG: solved 46% (SD 8.2); of correct, 56% insight vs 42% noninsight, t(18)=3.47, p=.003.
limits: Insight labels are self-report after the fact. Small samples. Problems are verbal (compound remote associates), not spatial.
agent_relevance: Insight is defined by solver report, so the only handle is a label after a solve; a model has no such label with ground truth.

source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Exp 1: insight solutions gave more fMRI signal than noninsight solutions in right anterior superior temporal gyrus (RH aSTG). The same region also rose when problems first appeared.
numbers: Peak voxel difference 0.25% over a 6 s window, 0.30% at one TR. Cluster 531 mm3, peak t=4.89 at Talairach (44,-9,-9). 12 of 13 subjects showed more signal for insight (0.03% to 0.35%). Onset-of-problem cluster 469 mm3, peak t=4.37.
limits: Cluster p<0.005 with a 13-subject sample. Temporal pole has fMRI dropout, so effects there cannot be ruled out. Effect is tiny in percent signal terms.
agent_relevance: Location is unreadable for a text-only agent; the useful idea is that insight reuses the same semantic region as normal solving, only stronger.

source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Exp 1 secondary insight effects were weaker: left medial frontal gyrus (453 mm3, peak diff 0.15%), small clusters near amygdala and parahippocampal gyrus (0.16%), left posterior cingulate. Inferior frontal gyrus (a priori region) was too small and unreliable to test left versus right.
numbers: IFG peak 0.21% at a lenient p<0.015; region signal only about 72% of brain average. No insight effect anywhere in left temporal cortex.
limits: Many did not reach the main threshold. IFG shown only at a relaxed threshold.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence for a frontal selection role; do not build rules on it.

source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Exp 2 EEG: a burst of gamma-band power (39 Hz) at right anterior temporal electrode T8 began about 0.3 s before the solution button press for insight solutions only.
numbers: Window -0.30 to -0.02 s: insight effect at T8 t(18)=3.48, p=.003; insight x time window F(1,18)=6.68, p=.019; insight x time window x hemisphere F(1,18)=8.11, p=.011; insight x hemisphere F(1,18)=4.61, p=.046. No effect at -1.52 to -0.36 s, none at left T7. Mean RT insight 9.94 s vs noninsight 9.25 s, t<1.
limits: Laplacian map used to localise; scalp EEG has coarse spatial resolution. One planned gamma test at one electrode pair and frequency. Scalp gamma is open to muscle artefact.
agent_relevance: Structural analogue for an agent: a sudden late jump in internal solution confidence rather than a gradual rise.

source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Exp 2 alpha result: insight trials had more alpha power at right parietal-occipital sites before the gamma burst, interpreted as gating visual input to let weak remote associations grow.
numbers: Alpha greater for insight in -1.31 to -0.56 s (9.8 Hz, right parietal-occipital); not in -2.06 to -1.56 s or -0.31 to +0.06 s. Theta and beta effects not significant; a 4 Hz frontal effect was confounded with eye movements.
limits: Alpha effect sat inside a slow alpha decline; the inhibition-of-vision reading is post hoc. Later work finds alpha elsewhere and in the opposite direction.
agent_relevance: Possible analogue: cut incoming distractor context while a weak association matures. A design idea, not evidence.

source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Theory (Beeman coarse semantic coding): left hemisphere codes fine, small, strong semantic fields; right hemisphere codes coarse, large, weak fields that overlap, so distant links can be joined. RH aSTG does that integration for insight.
numbers: Behavioural support cited: solution word weakly active in RH before awareness (Bowden and Jung-Beeman 2003). Solution times insight 10.25 s vs noninsight 11.28 s in Exp 1 (t<1, p>.3), so difficulty does not explain the RH effect.
quote: RH aSTG is also selectively active when subjects must generate the best ending to a sentence.
limits: Hemisphere story is simplified; later studies find left or bilateral effects (see a16, a11, a21).
agent_relevance: Coarse versus fine coding resembles wide versus narrow retrieval; no direct LLM test.

source: Jung-Beeman et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight (PLoS Biol)
finding: Stated logic for gamma: sudden all-or-none emergence predicts a discrete high-frequency burst. Earlier anagram response-time work (Smith and Kounios 1996) shows insight solutions appear in a discrete jump, not as partial outputs.
numbers: No numbers for that logic beyond Exp 2 above.
limits: Suddenness is inferred from behaviour plus one 0.3 s EEG window.
agent_relevance: Design principle: score insight as a discontinuity, not a gradient.

source: Kounios et al. (2008) The origins of insight in resting-state brain activity (Neuropsychologia)
finding: Resting EEG recorded before any task relates to later problem-solving style. Anagrams, 26 right-handed adults split by median into high-insight (HI) and low-insight (LI) groups.
numbers: N=26 (13 per group). HI mean insight-to-noninsight ratio 3.5 (SD 2.3); LI 0.8 (SD 0.4). 180 anagrams. 128-channel EEG, 3.5 min eyes-closed plus 3.5 min eyes-open rest. Overall solved 70.0% (SD 8.1), 56.1% (SD 19.2) with insight.
limits: Median split on a self-report ratio; small N; many ANOVAs with exploratory t-maps uncorrected for multiple comparisons (stated by authors).
agent_relevance: Style is trait-like in the solver. For an agent the analogue is the model or prompt default, not a readable online signal.

source: Kounios et al. (2008) The origins of insight in resting-state brain activity (Neuropsychologia)
finding: HI and LI solved equally well but differently: same accuracy, same RT, different error types. Insight style goes with errors of omission (timeouts), analytic style with errors of commission.
numbers: Correct: HI 68.9% vs LI 70.9%, t(24)=.60, p=.55. RT HI 5.19 s vs LI 5.10 s, t(24)=.28, p=.78. Errors HI 3.7% vs LI 4.9%, p=.30. Timeouts HI 27.4% vs LI 25.2%, p=.53.
limits: The omission versus commission link is an across-subject correlation.
agent_relevance: Matches the guess-versus-abstain tradeoff: an all-or-none solver abstains more than a partial-information solver.

source: Kounios et al. (2008) The origins of insight in resting-state brain activity (Neuropsychologia)
finding: Resting EEG group differences fit two hypotheses: HI had less occipital alpha (diffuse attention) and more right-lateralised activity at lateral frontal and parietal sites; LI had more occipital beta and more left inferior-frontal and anterior-temporal low-alpha.
numbers: Alpha AP x group F(3,72)=2.936, p=.049; High-alpha AP x group F(3,72)=4.811, p=.004; Beta-1 AP x group F(3,72)=7.011, p<.001; Gamma-1 E x DV x group F(1,24)=4.812, p=.038.
limits: Effects range p=.049 to p<.001 with uncorrected topographic follow-ups; no independent replication read.
agent_relevance: Background only. No online signal for a model; supports treating insight proneness as a stable trait.

source: Subramaniam et al. (2009) Aha! The neural correlates of verbal insight solutions (Hum Brain Mapp)
finding: Anagram fMRI with 10 usable people did not make right aSTG the top insight area. Insight versus search solutions activated right insula, left BA45, bilateral angular gyrus, right prefrontal BA10/46, anterior cingulate, and right temporal pole.
numbers: 12 recruited, 2 excluded for <20% insight or search solutions (N=10). Right PFC 534 voxels, t=4.77; anterior cingulate 1,513 voxels, t=6.08; right temporal pole 164 voxels, t=4.57; right insula 333 voxels, t=3.81. No voxel more active for search than insight.
limits: Very small N. Anagram task, not compound remote associates. Right temporal pole was found, but as a region deactivated by search and little activated by aha. Authors read ACC and insula as evaluation and metacognition.
agent_relevance: Insight-linked activity includes evaluation and monitoring: detecting a good solution may be a separate step from generating it.

source: Subramaniam et al. (2009) Aha! The neural correlates of verbal insight solutions (Hum Brain Mapp)
finding: Timing: right insula and left BA45 differed early (0-2.5 s from problem onset); angular gyri, ACC, pons, right temporal pole and right PFC differed late (3-5.5 s).
numbers: Half-second time points; hemodynamic lag not removed.
limits: Time-resolved fMRI is coarse; timing claims are weak.
agent_relevance: Early language-network divergence then late monitoring is a plausible two-stage story.

source: Sandkuhler and Bhattacharya (2008) Deconstructing insight: EEG correlates of insightful problem solving (PLoS ONE)
finding: Independent EEG study on compound remote associates separating features of insight: impasse, restructuring, suddenness. Found gamma at parieto-occipital sites tied to impasse and attention, upper alpha in right temporal region for hinted solves, decreased alpha in right prefrontal for high restructuring.
numbers: Correct solves without hint 38.8% (SD 9.6); incorrect 11.2% (SD 8.0); hint trials 39.4% correct. Median trials per person: sudden correct 17 (4-32), non-sudden 1 (0-8), full restructuring 4 (0-21). Suddenness vs restructuring rho=-0.39, t(18)=-5.17, p<0.0001.
limits: Hints used to induce restructuring; ratings are subjective; about 19 people; very few non-sudden or fully restructured trials.
agent_relevance: Sudden solutions involve little reported restructuring. The feeling of suddenness is not evidence of restructuring work.

source: Sandkuhler and Bhattacharya (2008) Deconstructing insight: EEG correlates of insightful problem solving (PLoS ONE)
finding: Different locus than Jung-Beeman: impasse-linked gamma sits over parieto-occipital cortex, not right anterior temporal. Right parieto-occipital gamma was higher before the hint for impasse that ended in timeout than for impasse that ended in a solution.
numbers: Impasse theta effect (4-8 Hz) over parieto-occipital sites from -2.25 to -1.5 s before the impasse.
limits: Authors read gamma as selective-attention overload at impasse: a competing reading of gamma.
agent_relevance: Impasse may reflect over-focus on one representation: supports forcing a re-frame after repeated failure.

source: Sandkuhler and Bhattacharya (2008) Deconstructing insight: EEG correlates of insightful problem solving (PLoS ONE)
finding: Cluster-based permutation tests in space x time x frequency. Upper alpha rose in right temporal regions for trials unsolved before the hint and solved after it, read as suppressing weakly active solution information. Alpha fell in right prefrontal for high restructuring.
numbers: 55.6% of hint-free correct solves had high suddenness (>=2) with low restructuring (<=1); 23.3% had both high.
limits: Alpha reading (suppress solution information) differs from Jung-Beeman (gate vision).
agent_relevance: Competing alpha accounts show the alpha result is unstable across studies.

source: Hum Brain Mapp (2024) Time course of EEG power during creative problem-solving with insight or remote thinking
finding: Partial replication in French with a compound associate task (CAT). Eureka trials showed alpha then gamma increase before the response, but in a LEFT temporal cluster, plus frontal theta.
numbers: N=21 (23 recruited, 2 excluded). Accuracy 57.4% (SD 12.0), mean RT 8.4 s; Eureka on 55.6% of correct trials. Alpha cluster left central/temporal -1.96 to -1.55 s (13 electrodes, sum(t)=1174, p corr=.01). About 30 usable insight-analysis trials per person.
limits: Few trials; correct trials only; fixed windows ignore the middle of each trial; sensor-level clusters. Left not right: so a partial, not clean, replication.
agent_relevance: The alpha-then-gamma order replicates; the right-hemisphere claim does not in this study.

source: Hum Brain Mapp (2024) Time course of EEG power during creative problem-solving with insight or remote thinking
finding: Semantic remoteness of the solution (low association strength) raised alpha (left parieto-temporal), early beta (right fronto-temporal) and late theta (bilateral frontal). Remote solutions were harder and slower.
numbers: Association strength vs accuracy beta=.11 (SD .04), t(20)=12.04, p=1.29e-10; vs RT beta=-.07 (SD .07), t(20)=-4.64, p=1.58e-4. No positive clusters for remoteness.
limits: First EEG test of remoteness per the authors; one lab, one language.
agent_relevance: Remoteness is a measurable input property. A model can compute it from embeddings, unlike brain power.

source: Ogawa, Aihara and Yamashita (2025) Neural correlates and dynamical brain states of creative insight in a spatial problem task (Sci Rep)
finding: Spatial matchstick-arithmetic fMRI, 16 people. Default mode network was more active for insight solves than for quick or analytical solves; executive control network more active for quick and analytical. Right superior temporal pole and left SFG appeared for insight over analytical.
numbers: N=16 (1 excluded: no insight). Of 2,780 trials: quick 1,686, analytical 735, insight 134 (mean 8.4 per person). RT quick 8.61 s, analytical 36.58 s, insight 114.44 s. Hit rate quick 97.9%, analytical 96.7%, insight 78.6% (SD 27.8). GLM at uncorrected p=0.001.
limits: Very few insight trials; insight RT 114 s is far from 10 s verbal trials; uncorrected threshold; spatial not verbal task.
agent_relevance: Different tasks give different networks, so there is no single insight signature. Reinforces: no portable online signal.

source: Aihara and colleagues (2017) Anodal tDCS of the right anterior temporal lobe did not significantly affect verbal or non-verbal insight (PLoS ONE)
finding: Failed causal replication. Stimulating right ATL (anodal) did not improve insight in a within-subject design.
numbers: 66 subjects, two days, active versus sham, two montages (right ATL anodal with left ATL cathodal; right ATL anodal with left cheek cathodal). Extra-cephalic montage effect size 0.21 non-verbal, about 0 verbal; verbal effect sizes negative for bi-cephalic montage; no significant differences.
limits: Non-verbal arm underpowered (two problems; only 3 people solved one type). Stimulation focality uncertain. No effect is not proof of no role.
agent_relevance: Warning: right ATL as the locus of insight is not causally supported. Do not bake a hemisphere rule into the agent.

source: Meta-analysis of fMRI studies in divergent thinking and insight (Hum Brain Mapp 2022)
finding: ALE meta-analysis of 27 divergent-thinking and 30 insight fMRI studies. Insight engaged precentral gyrus, IFG, parahippocampal gyrus, amygdala, superior parietal lobe. Divergent thinking engaged inferior parietal lobe, cuneus, MFG. Conjunction found no overlap.
numbers: 27 DT studies and 30 insight studies. Insight > DT in IFG, MFG, parahippocampal gyrus, amygdala; DT > insight in inferior parietal lobe.
limits: Abstract does not name right anterior temporal lobe as a core insight region; pooled tasks are mixed (verbal, spatial, riddles). Only the abstract and results summary were read.
agent_relevance: Meta-analytic picture favours executive and emotion regions, so right temporal alone is too narrow to build on.

source: Salvi, Luchini, Pestilli, Hanekamp, Parrish, Beeman and Grafman (2026) The white matter of Aha! moments (BMC Psychology)
finding: Diffusion imaging: individual tendency to solve compound remote associates by insight versus analysis related to LEFT dorsal white-matter tracts (arcuate, posterior arcuate, SLF III), not right.
numbers: Left dorsal tract FA composites significant after Stouffer Z and FDR; mean diffusivity trended (p=0.032, q=0.081). Controlled for age and gender.
limits: Sample size not recorded here; correlational; MD not significant after correction.
agent_relevance: Another left-lateralised result, even with a founding-team coauthor, against a pure right-hemisphere story.

source: Kim (2026) Illumination Onset: A Theoretical Neuroscience Framework for the Sudden Aha Moment (Behav Sci)
finding: Theory paper reading the literature as alpha decrease and gamma increase near reported solutions, called dominance inversion, tied to precision weighting in predictive processing, ACC surprise detection and serotonin.
numbers: No new data. Cites the 2024 Hum Brain Mapp EEG study and Bowden et al. 2005.
limits: Theoretical. The alpha-decrease reading conflicts with Jung-Beeman 2004 (alpha rose) and agrees with Sandkuhler 2008 for high restructuring.
agent_relevance: Predictive-processing view: insight is a reweighting of prior against new evidence, a metaphor for lowering prior dominance after failed attempts.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models (arXiv 2601.00514)
finding: Tests whether reasoning LLMs have real Aha moments mid-trace. Over 1M reasoning traces and hundreds of checkpoints, mid-reasoning shifts were rare, did not grow with training, and seldom raised accuracy. Forcing shifts under high entropy did raise accuracy.
numbers: 1M+ traces, hundreds of checkpoints, 3 reasoning domains, several temperatures and architectures. Abstract gives no percentages.
limits: Abstract only. Shift definition is theirs. Not a neural measure.
agent_relevance: Do not trust an in-trace aha as insight. Trigger re-framing from an entropy or stuck signal in code, not from model self-report.

source: Wu et al. (2025) Aha Moment Revisited: Are VLMs Truly Capable of Self Verification in Inference-time Scaling? (arXiv 2506.17417)
finding: In RL-tuned vision-language models, majority voting beat verification-centric best-of-N with self-verification, and aha-like behaviours did not reliably improve reasoning.
numbers: Abstract gives no numbers.
limits: Abstract only. Vision-language models and visual math, not insight problems.
agent_relevance: Supports voting over self-verification; supports keeping judgement outside the model.

source: arXiv listing search (page summary) 2025-2026 on aha moments in reasoning models
finding: A search page listed 37 papers; only the summary was read. Entries include Illusion of Insight (2601.00514), Reasoning Theater (2603.05488; answers decodable before the CoT shows them), EvolMathEval (2508.13003; blames errors on a pseudo aha moment), Aha-Flow Distillation (2609.07036), EvoThink (2607.19962).
numbers: Second-hand figures: EvolMathEval 77% to 100% of errors on targeted problems from a pseudo aha moment; Double-Checker AIME pass@1 4.4% to 18.2%.
limits: Not opened. Verify before citing. Ids and years come from the listing page.
agent_relevance: Candidates for the LLM-evidence angle; none tests a neural signature.

source: Bowden and Jung-Beeman (2003) Aha! Insight experience correlates with solution activation in the right hemisphere (Psychon Bull Rev)
finding: Lateralised priming: solution words shown to the left visual field (right hemisphere) were primed more for insight than for noninsight solutions.
numbers: Not opened. Described in Subramaniam 2009 and Jung-Beeman 2004 only as: solution activated subconsciously in RH before conscious retrieval, only for aha solutions.
limits: Not read; numbers not recorded.
agent_relevance: Behavioural root of the right-hemisphere claim.

source: Kounios et al. (2006) The prepared mind: neural activity prior to problem presentation predicts subsequent solution type (Psychol Sci)
finding: Pre-problem EEG activity predicted whether the later solution would be insight or analytic (cited in Kounios 2008 as transient preparatory activity).
numbers: Not opened; numbers not recorded.
limits: Known only through Kounios 2008 in this session.
agent_relevance: Insight versus analytic strategy is partly set before the problem arrives, like a prompt-level prior.

source: Kounios and Beeman (2009) The Aha! moment: the cognitive neuroscience of insight (Curr Dir Psychol Sci)
finding: Review of the line: RH anterior temporal gamma burst, preceding alpha, resting-state and preparatory differences. Named in the subfield row.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Pointer only, not evidence.
